questions.question: In the STAR analysis, what event-mixing construction isolates the soft-soft three-particle background?

options.A: Keep the two associates from the same event but take the trigger from another event in the same centrality window
options.B: Mix trigger and associates across events, adding trigger flow pairwise
options.C: Mix all three particles from one event and subtract the measured v2
options.D: Fold two jet-like correlations and normalize at the away-side peak

questions.rationale: The associates remain from one event so their mutual correlations independent of the trigger are retained; the trigger comes from another event.
questions.evidence_quote: This background is obtained from mixed events

questions.question: How was the non-Poisson multiplicity factor β determined in the background subtraction?

options.A: By requiring the subtracted triplet yield to equal the inclusive event multiplicity
options.B: By equating the background-subtracted jet-like pair yield with the square of the single-associate yield
options.C: By fitting the away-side peak width in pp and d+Au simultaneously
options.D: By scaling the mixed-event v4 term to 1.15 times the measured v2

questions.rationale: β was set through a yield consistency relation between the three- and two-particle jet-like signals.
questions.evidence_quote: the number of associated pairs in the background subtracted jet-like three-particle correlation signal equals the square of the number of associated particles

questions.question: Which centrality-dependent pattern distinguished the candidate conical signal from the away-side broadening?

options.A: A near-side peak shifted progressively away from zero in peripheral Au+Au
options.B: A diagonal peak at π disappeared in the highest-statistics central bin
options.C: An off-diagonal structure near π ± 1.45 radians grew with centrality
options.D: The pp away-side peak became narrower than the d+Au peak

questions.rationale: The paper reports a growing off-diagonal structure in more central Au+Au collisions, prominent in top-12% ZDC data.
questions.evidence_quote: the more central Au+Au collisions display an off-diagonal structure, at about π ± 1.45 radians

questions.question: What did the measured associated-pT dependence of the off-diagonal angle imply for the two proposed emission mechanisms?

options.A: A sharply decreasing angle supported Cherenkov radiation over hydrodynamics
options.B: A linear increase favored deﬂected jets over conical emission
options.C: No angle could be extracted because the signal vanished above 1 GeV/c
options.D: A constant angle was observed, consistent with Mach-cone emission rather than the cited simple Cherenkov prediction

questions.rationale: The analysis found no strong pT dependence; the cited simple Cherenkov model predicts a sharply decreasing angle with increasing associated pT.
questions.evidence_quote: The angle is consistent with constant as a function of associated particle pT.

questions.question: What normalization prescription was used for the two-particle background in the default analysis?

options.A: Normalize the mixed-event background to the signal in 0.8 < |Δφ| < 1.2 (ZYA1)
options.B: Normalize at the near-side peak over |Δφ| < 0.2
options.C: Normalize to the integral over the full azimuthal range
options.D: Normalize the background in 0.6 < |Δφ| < 1.4 from the outset

questions.rationale: The default scaling α used zero yield at one radian; widening that window was only a systematic check.
questions.evidence_quote: scale factor α) to the signal within

questions.question: How did the authors estimate the systematic uncertainty from elliptic-flow subtraction?

options.A: They varied v2 from zero to the inclusive charged-particle yield
options.B: They used reaction-plane and four-particle-cumulant v2 values as upper and lower bounds
options.C: They replaced v2 with v4 and assigned the resulting difference
options.D: They compared only pp and d+Au since neither has flow

questions.rationale: The default used an average of the two v2 measurements, and their separate values bounded the systematic.
questions.evidence_quote: We use the reaction plane and 4-particle cumulant v2 as the upper and lower bounds

questions.question: What was the measured location of the off-diagonal peaks from the double-Gaussian projection fit?
questions.rationale: The fitted off-diagonal locations were reported as 1.45 radians from π.
questions.evidence_quote: were found to be 1.45 radians from π.

questions.question: Why could the on-diagonal/off-diagonal signal difference be interpreted as evidence about deflected jets?

options.A: Both regions contain only deflected-jet contributions, but have different acceptance
options.B: The off-diagonal region is a pure flow background and the on-diagonal region is pure jet signal
options.C: The difference directly measures the v4 normalization uncertainty
options.D: Conical emission is expected to be equal in both regions, while only the on-diagonal region can also contain deflected jets

questions.rationale: The paper states that the off-diagonal signal can contain conical emission only, whereas the on-diagonal can include deflected jets too.

questions.question: Which sensitivity check addressed the α normalization window, and what was its reported implication?

options.A: The window was doubled to 0.6 < |Δφ| < 1.4, and the signal remained robust
options.B: The window was narrowed to 0.9–1.1 rad, and the signal disappeared
options.C: The window was moved to π, producing a sign reversal
options.D: The normalization was removed, and only the near-side peak survived

questions.rationale: Doubling the normalization window was a systematic test and did not materially change the signal.
questions.evidence_quote: the size of the normalization window was doubled to 0.6 < |∆φ| < 1.4. The signal is robust

questions.question: What was the principal caveat in the paper's interpretation of the central Au+Au off-diagonal peaks?

options.A: They conclusively measured a Mach cone and excluded all other mechanisms
options.B: They were consistent with conical emission and with Mach-cone expectations, but were not definitive proof of a Mach cone
options.C: They appeared equally in pp, d+Au, and Au+Au, preventing medium interpretation
options.D: Their angle varied strongly with pT, proving Cherenkov radiation

questions.rationale: The authors describe the structures as consistent with conical emission and say the pT result is consistent with Mach-cone emission, not as conclusive identification.
questions.evidence_quote: Oﬀ-diagonal peaks consistent with conical emission are present in central Au+Au collisions.
